newsitem.title: USA: PDVSA mulls concession on controversial muni taxes.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA mulls concession on controversial muni taxes.

text.p: Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) is considering a move that would alleviate some of the worries over local tax which have been hampering investment by international oil companies.

The Venezuelan state oil company, putting the final touches on a new contract for its third tender for "marginal fields," is considering partially reimbursing investors for municipal taxes, a top PdVSA official confirmed on Wednesday.
Officials from companies that plan to participate in the tender say that PDVSA has already agreed in principle to reimburse contractors for any municipal tax in excess of four percent.
"(The reimbursement) hasn't been accepted yet. It's a suggestion that's being considered," Juan Szabo, a senior PdVSA official, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Uncertainty about municipal tax rates and their effect on profits have long been among the major concerns of private investors eyeing Venezuela's vast upstream potential.

Even if PDVSA agrees to the current proposal for round three of the marginal field sales, other investors in planned multi-billion dollar joint ventures and profit-sharing contracts would still be subject to the unpredictable levy.
One investor suggested that the companies should work together on this and other outstanding issues such as dollar tax accounting and asset-depreciation rules to show Caracas that they're serious.

"(PDVSA) thinks the companies are bluffing...but the companies don't send a clear signal either," he said. "On the one hand, they complain and complain. On the other hand, they continue with their work."
Szabo said a final operating contract for the upcoming tender as well as a protocol document outlining logistical details of the auction would be released on April 21.
Some 200 foreign and local companies have prequalified to participate in the tender. Up for grabs are 20 areas that are no longer producing significant amounts of oil.

PDVSA has pegged total investment at around $4.6 billion over 10 years. Production from the areas is forecast to rise to at least 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) from current levels of around 66,000 bpd.
Bidding is scheduled for June 2-6. About four areas will be auctioned each day, with awards based on cash offers.

Venezuela, a founding member of the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), has been courting investors to help double oil production to more than six million bpd in 10 years. --Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((212 859 1620))
